event.name: Readathon 2026
event.subtitle: The Crucible
event.tagline: Your character class against every other. Books — and glory — on the line.
event.timezoneNote: You may start in your timezone, or start in Mountain Time.
lore: Welcome to the Readathon 2026. All the realms have been destroyed — you are being forced into The Crucible, a deadly competition where it's your character class against every other character class.
The strongest will put their books (and lives) on the line to gain XP, leveling themselves and their team up while sabotaging the XP of other teams.
First things first: you'll need a team before you're shipped off to the competition. Once accepted, you'll be sorted into one of four realms.

bonusPrompts.label: A guilty pleasure — a book that provides comfort to you
A story centred around good vs evil
A book with a school/academic setting
A book with foiling on the cover
An author you've read from before
A book with a mystery element
Steal a book from someone's March TBR that is not your team

globalBonuses.label: Competition / trials in the book
globalBonuses.description: The story involves a competition or trials.

positive.label: A book you didn't buy
positive.description: You didn't purchase this — e.g. library, KU (book returns after). Not an Audible credit where you keep it forever.

positive.label: A fast-paced read
positive.description: Your interpretation of a story that moves quickly.

positive.label: Read a sequel
positive.description: A sequel to a previous book.

positive.label: Multiple POVs
positive.description: A book with more than one point of view.

positive.label: Different format than your last book
positive.description: If you read an ebook for your last book, this must be audio or physical (and vice versa).

positive.label: Read an author's backlist
positive.description: Not the author's most recent release. Even if it came out 20 years ago, if it's their most recent book published it doesn't count. Any other book by that author counts.

positive.label: Randomize your TBR with a die
positive.description: Randomize which book you pick — titles to numbers, shelves to numbers, etc.

positive.label: Structural openings on the cover
positive.description: A door, window, gate, etc. on the cover.

positive.label: Second chances
positive.description: Reread a book, retry an author/book, or a second chance romance.

positive.label: Author's name is two lines on the cover
positive.description: Author's name is two lines — NOT one — on the cover.

positive.label: A book with parts
positive.description: The book is split up into parts.

positive.label: Read a host's 5-star read
positive.description: Does not have to be your team's host — any of the 9 hosts.

positive.label: Own voices
positive.description: An author from a marginalized group writing from their lived experience.

positive.label: Symbols in the title
positive.description: Things like & or ' in the title.

negative.label: Start a series
negative.description: First book in a series, not a sequel.

negative.label: Read a recent haul instead of your TBR
negative.description: A book you recently acquired, not from your planned TBR.

negative.label: More pages than your last book
negative.description: Must have more pages than the book you just finished.

negative.label: A 5-star prediction
negative.description: A book you think you might give 5 stars.

negative.label: A character has a hidden identity
negative.description: Character is hiding who they are or a secret from the reader or other characters.

negative.label: Read a book in one sitting
Author writes in multiple genres
negative.description: The author writes across multiple genres.

negative.label: No "THE" anywhere in the title
negative.description: Including as the first word — no "the" anywhere.

negative.label: Roll a D6 for words in the title
negative.description: Whatever the die lands on is how many words your title must have.

negative.label: POC author
negative.description: The author is a person of colour.

negative.label: Interconnected world/series
negative.description: Another series exists in the same world (e.g. Cosmere). Interconnected standalones within the same series do NOT count.

negative.label: Icon between title and author on spine
negative.description: There is an icon between the title and author on the spine.

howItWorks.title: Join the Crucible
howItWorks.body: Sign up with your name and email. You'll wait in the pool until teams are assigned.

howItWorks.title: Get sorted into a realm
howItWorks.body: Once accepted, you'll be randomly placed on one of four teams.

howItWorks.title: Read & submit
howItWorks.body: Finish a book, then use the submission form. Pick up to 5 prompts — all positive OR all negative per book.

howItWorks.title: Add or sabotage
howItWorks.body: Help your team's XP or attack another realm. One book can only do one — not both.

howItWorks.title: Layer bonuses
howItWorks.body: Team prompts, page-count bonuses, and competition/trials stack on top of your 5 prompts.

howItWorks.title: Double-check
howItWorks.body: Submissions cannot be edited. Review carefully before you submit!

faq.q: Can I use more than one prompt?
faq.a: Yes — up to five prompts per book, not including bonus prompts. They must all be increasing OR all decreasing.
If you think it counts, count it. If you think it doesn't, don't.

faq.q: Do I have to read my realm's bonus prompts?
faq.a: No — they're optional extras for people who want them.

faq.q: How do I track my reads?
faq.a: Use the submission form on this site after your team is assigned.

faq.q: How many times can bonus prompts be used?
faq.a: As many times as you like.
Yes — use them as much as you want.
One book attacks one realm. Your next book can target a different realm.

faq.q: Can one book both increase and decrease?
faq.a: No — one book does one or the other.

faq.q: How is it fair if one realm has more members?
faq.a: Points are averaged per person on the team.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of prompts?
faq.a: Nope — do as many or as few as you'd like.

faq.q: Do manga or graphic novels count?
faq.a: Yes — any form of reading counts.

faq.q: Can a book started in February but finished in March count?
faq.a: Use your discretion. If you only read 10 pages in March, probably not. A good chunk in March — sure.

faq.q: Can a book be a re-read?

faq.a: Use your discretion — if you read a good chunk in March, sure.
Use Goodreads page count. If none, use 40 pages per hour.
Be fair about what you'd accept from others. A five-page short story probably isn't fair.

faq.q: Do bonus prompts count toward the five?
faq.a: No — you get 5 prompts, then bonuses layer on top.
